acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Serpents family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Horned Viper, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Buried-Reach Champion archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Massive sand-adapted viper with paired eye horns, heavy keeled scales, thick tail, and multiple old shed scars.
Signature mechanic: Horn Gates: paired eye horns surface at alternating points while the tail indicates the gap opposite the real opening.
battlefieldDuty: Attack through alternating horn-marked emergence points while its exposed tail controls the safe route.
constructionDimensions: Mineral scutes reinforce the brow, belly anchor, horn, and selected crown plates while flexible scale bands stay visible.
Coils compress sediment and lift detached chips along their exact load path rather than becoming solid stone.
counterplay: Follow the tail direction to locate the real opening and punish the emerging neck after evading. Affinity signal: A pale fracture line opens at the neck, belly anchor, buried emergence plate, or loosened crown scale.
forbiddenTreatments: Mineral plates that fuse separate coils into an unreadable mass
identityInvariants: Every form remains limbless with a continuous scaled body, snake skull, jaw hinge, belly scutes, forked tongue, and species-appropriate tail.
Tier escalation uses body proportion, hood, fangs, horns, crown scales, muscle distribution, and coil behavior rather than arms or equipment.
Strike range, head anchor, venom direction, emergence point, and loosened coil remain visually traceable.
telegraph: One horn breaks the surface before each head strike and the exposed tail points away from it.
